### 1.1 Purpose Statement

This standard establishes mandatory requirements for Configuration Item (CI) discovery functionality within the enterprise. CI discovery is the automated process of identifying, collecting, and maintaining accurate information about infrastructure components, applications, and their relationships in the Configuration Management Database (CMDB).

The standard defines requirements for both agent-based and agentless discovery methods, ensuring comprehensive coverage of all enterprise infrastructure while maintaining security, performance, and data quality standards. Effective CI discovery is foundational to maintaining the CMDB as a single source of truth for IT asset and configuration information.
page_texts.6:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#12-scope]

### 1.2 Scope

**In Scope:**

- Agent-based discovery deployment and configuration standards
- Agentless discovery protocols, credentials, and access requirements
- Discovery scheduling, frequency, and coverage requirements
- Discovery data classification and attribute collection standards
- Integration of discovery data with the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)
- Discovery of physical, virtual, and cloud infrastructure components
- Application and service discovery requirements
- Network device and connection discovery
- Dependency and relationship discovery

**Out of Scope:**

- Discovery tool vendor selection (governed by procurement processes)
- CMDB schema design (governed by separate data architecture standards)
- Discovery of non-IT assets such as facilities and furniture
- End-user personal devices not connected to enterprise networks
- Discovery tool licensing and cost management

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#13-compliance-level]

### 1.3 Compliance Level

**MANDATORY** - All infrastructure components, applications, and services within the enterprise environment MUST be subject to automated CI discovery using approved methods. Discovery coverage gaps require documented exceptions with approved remediation plans.
page_texts.8:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#14-business-rationale]

### 1.4 Business Rationale

Manual CI data entry is error-prone, labor-intensive, and cannot keep pace with dynamic infrastructure environments. CI discovery automation provides the foundation for accurate, timely CMDB data that supports critical ITSM processes.

**Business Impact of Inadequate CI Discovery:**

| Impact Area | Consequence | Business Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Asset Visibility | Unknown or undiscovered infrastructure creates security blind spots | 68% of security breaches involve unknown assets |
| Change Management | Incomplete CI data leads to failed impact assessments | Major incidents increase 40% with discovery gaps |
| License Compliance | Undiscovered software creates compliance risk | Software audit penalties average $250K per occurrence |
| Cost Management | Shadow IT and orphaned resources go untracked | 25-30% of cloud spend typically wasted on unused resources |
| Service Mapping | Incomplete relationships prevent accurate service views | Service restoration times increase 3x with poor dependency data |

Implementing comprehensive CI discovery ensures the CMDB reflects the actual state of the enterprise environment, enabling informed decision-making across all ITSM processes.

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#31-agent-based-discovery]

### 3.1 Agent-Based Discovery

Agent-based discovery deploys software agents on target systems that collect and report configuration information to a central discovery server.
page_texts.32:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#311-how-agent-based-discovery-works]

#### 3.1.1 How Agent-Based Discovery Works

| Component | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Discovery Agent | Software installed on target system; collects local configuration data |
| Agent Manager | Central server managing agent deployment, configuration, and updates |
| Communication Protocol | Secure channel (typically HTTPS) for agent-to-server communication |
| Discovery Policies | Rules defining what data to collect and how frequently |
page_texts.33:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#312-agent-based-discovery-advantages]

#### 3.1.2 Agent-Based Discovery Advantages

| Advantage | Description | Best Use Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deep Data Collection | Access to local system information not available remotely | Detailed software inventory, process-level data |
| Firewall Friendly | Outbound agent communication traverses firewalls easily | Distributed environments, remote sites |
| Real-Time Capability | Agents can report changes as they occur | Dynamic environments requiring immediate visibility |
| Offline Capability | Agents cache data when network unavailable | Systems with intermittent connectivity |
| Lower Remote Privileges | No need for remote administrative credentials | Environments with strict credential policies |
page_texts.34:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#313-agent-based-discovery-considerations]

#### 3.1.3 Agent-Based Discovery Considerations

| Consideration | Description | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent Deployment | Requires installation on each target system | Automated deployment via SCCM, Intune, or equivalent |
| System Resources | Agents consume CPU, memory, and disk | Lightweight agent design; scheduled collection windows |
| Agent Maintenance | Updates and patches required | Centralized agent management and auto-update |
| Platform Coverage | Agent must support target OS/platform | Verify platform support before deployment |
page_texts.35:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#314-agent-based-discovery-requirements]

#### 3.1.4 Agent-Based Discovery Requirements

| Requirement | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Agent Resource Limit | Less than 1% CPU average, 100MB maximum memory |
| Communication Security | TLS 1.2 minimum, certificate validation required |
| Update Mechanism | Automated agent updates with rollback capability |
| Failure Handling | Graceful degradation; no system impact on agent failure |

### 3.3 Method Selection Criteria

Use the following decision criteria to select appropriate discovery methods:
page_texts.43:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#331-agent-based-discovery-selection]

#### 3.3.1 Agent-Based Discovery Selection

Deploy agent-based discovery when:

| Criterion | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| Deep software inventory required | Agents provide detailed installed software, processes, and files |
| Real-time change detection needed | Agent event-driven reporting faster than scheduled agentless scans |
| Distributed environment | Agents communicate outbound, simplifying firewall traversal |
| Credential restrictions | Agent eliminates need for remote administrative credentials |
| Intermittent connectivity | Agent can cache and forward when reconnected |
page_texts.44:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#332-agentless-discovery-selection]

#### 3.3.2 Agentless Discovery Selection

Deploy agentless discovery when:

| Criterion | Rationale |
| --- | --- |
| Agent installation not possible | Legacy systems, appliances, network devices |
| Resource constraints | No additional software footprint on target systems |
| Rapid deployment required | Immediate discovery without agent rollout |
| Read-only requirement | Agentless avoids any software modification |
| Network device discovery | SNMP standard for network equipment |
| Cloud infrastructure | Native APIs provide comprehensive cloud discovery |
page_texts.45:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#333-decision-matrix]

#### 3.3.3 Decision Matrix

| System Type | Recommended Method | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Servers | Agent + Agentless | Agent for depth, agentless for coverage validation |
| Linux Servers | Agent + Agentless | Agent for application detail, agentless for baseline |
| Network Devices | Agentless Only | Cannot run agents; SNMP/SSH standard |
| Cloud Infrastructure | Agentless (API) | Native APIs provide authoritative cloud data |
| Virtual Infrastructure | Agentless (API) | VMware/Hyper-V APIs for hypervisor-level data |
| Containers/Kubernetes | Agentless (API) | Kubernetes API for dynamic container discovery |
| Workstations | Agent Only | Distributed, intermittent connectivity |
| Legacy/Embedded | Agentless | Often cannot support agents |
| Database Servers | Agent + Agentless | Agent for instance detail, agentless for presence |
page_texts.46:

### 3.4 Hybrid Discovery Strategy

The recommended enterprise approach combines both methods for comprehensive coverage.
page_texts.47:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#341-hybrid-strategy-benefits]

#### 3.4.1 Hybrid Strategy Benefits

| Benefit | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Complete Coverage | All CI types can be discovered using appropriate method |
| Data Validation | Cross-validate data between agent and agentless sources |
| Resilience | Backup discovery method if primary method fails |
| Optimal Depth | Deep data from agents, broad coverage from agentless |
page_texts.48:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#342-hybrid-data-reconciliation]

#### 3.4.2 Hybrid Data Reconciliation

When both methods discover the same CI, apply these rules:

| Attribute Type | Authoritative Source | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hardware Specifications | Agentless (hypervisor/BIOS level) | More authoritative for virtualized environments |
| Installed Software | Agent | More complete local software visibility |
| Network Configuration | Agentless | Validates actual network connectivity |
| Process/Service Details | Agent | Real-time local process visibility |
| Cloud Resource Attributes | Agentless (Cloud API) | Authoritative cloud provider data |

All discovery data must route through the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) per [STD-OPS-CMDB-001](STD-OPS-CMDB-001-identification-reconciliation-engine.md) for deduplication and reconciliation.

Discovery scans MUST execute at minimum required frequencies:

| --- | --- | --- |
| Production Servers | Daily | Critical infrastructure requires current data |

### 9.1 Zero Trust Alignment

CI discovery infrastructure must align with Zero Trust architecture principles per [GUID-SEC-ZERO-TRUST-001](../../strategy/guidance/security/GUID-SEC-ZERO%20TRUST%20ARCH-REF-0.0.02.md). Discovery systems have privileged access across the enterprise and represent high-value targets for adversaries.
page_texts.121:
[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#zero-trust-principles-applied-to-discovery]

#### Zero Trust Principles Applied to Discovery

| Principle | Application to Discovery | Implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Never Trust, Always Verify | Every discovery request authenticated regardless of network location | mTLS for agents; OAuth 2.0 + DPoP for APIs; SNMP v3 auth |
| Least Privilege Access | Discovery accounts have minimum permissions for specific CI classes | Granular RBAC; no domain admin; read-only where possible |
| Assume Breach | Discovery infrastructure segmented; lateral movement prevention | Network micro-segmentation; dedicated management VLAN |
| Continuous Monitoring | All discovery activity logged and analyzed for anomalies | SIEM integration; behavioral analytics; real-time alerting |
| Data-Centric Security | Discovered data protected based on classification | Encryption; access controls; data minimization |

[standards/itsm-operations/STD-OPS-CMDB-002-ci-discovery.md#zero-trust-implementation-checklist]

#### Zero Trust Implementation Checklist

- [ ] Discovery servers deployed in dedicated network segment
- [ ] All discovery communications encrypted (TLS 1.2+ minimum)
- [ ] mTLS enabled for agent-to-server communication
- [ ] Service accounts provisioned through identity governance
- [ ] Just-in-time access implemented for privileged operations
- [ ] Continuous monitoring enabled with SIEM integration
- [ ] Network micro-segmentation prevents lateral movement
- [ ] Policy Decision Point validates all access requests
